steps.name: Library size, PCA, sample-distance QC and sample_01 verdict
caveats: sample_01's low library size can distort both size-factor estimation and vst variance stabilization at low counts, artificially inflating or deflating its apparent distance from other samples — check whether its outlier appearance (if any) is driven by real biological difference or by technical shot noise at low depth
Do not drop sample_01 automatically; this step only characterizes and recommends, since exclusion decisions affect the (out-of-scope-here) downstream DE step and design balance (would leave 5 vs 6)
Use raw counts for library size (column sums), not normalized values
Apply a minimal low-count gene filter (e.g., genes with count >=10 in at least a few samples) before PCA/vst so a shallow sample does not dominate variance via all-zero/near-zero genes
steps.context: Input: /eval-full-32-without-qc-only-n6-1/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (raw Salmon gene-level integer counts, 12000 genes x 12 samples, first column gene symbol) and /eval-full-32-without-qc-only-n6-1/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv (12 samples x condition: AD lesional vs control, unpaired, single batch). This is a pre-DE quality-control characterization only — no differential expression testing is requested here. sample_01 is flagged in the data profile as having a library size about 4x below the median; the step must independently verify this from the counts and assess its impact on PCA/clustering behavior rather than assuming it is problematic.
steps.question: Across the 12 skin samples (6 AD lesional vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch), what are the per-sample library sizes, how do samples separate in a PCA of normalized expression, what does the sample-to-sample distance matrix show, and does sample_01 (flagged with a library size ~4x below the median) look like a true outlier that should be flagged or excluded from downstream DE testing?

grounding.reason: Standard DESeq2 QC workflow (size factors, vst, PCA, sample distance heatmap) for a bulk RNA-seq count matrix; no knowledge_recommend tool was attached in this session.

constraints: Use DESeq2's median-of-ratios size factors and vst (or rlog if vst is unstable given n=12) for the PCA and distance matrix — do not use raw or simple CPM values for these two outputs
Report library sizes from raw counts.csv column sums, independent of normalization
Label all samples by both sample ID and condition in every plot so sample_01 is traceable
Keep the verdict evidence-based: state explicitly whether PCA/distance evidence supports or contradicts the library-size-based concern about sample_01
acceptance_criteria: Reports total raw read/count library size for all 12 samples (from counts.csv), explicitly quantifying sample_01's library size relative to the cohort median and confirming or refining the ~4x-below-median flag

Produces a PCA plot (PC1 vs PC2, with % variance explained) on DESeq2 size-factor-normalized and vst/rlog-transformed counts, colored by condition (AD lesional vs control), with sample labels visible so sample_01's position is identifiable
Produces a sample-to-sample Euclidean (or Poisson) distance matrix/heatmap with hierarchical clustering across all 12 samples on the same normalized data used for PCA

Gives an explicit verdict on sample_01: whether it clusters as an outlier in PCA and/or distance matrix consistent with its low library size, and a concrete recommendation (retain, retain with caveat, or exclude from downstream DE) grounded in the observed PCA/distance behavior rather than the library-size flag alone
Reports how many of the 12000 genes remain after any low-count filtering applied prior to PCA/vst, and states the filtering rule used
All outputs (library size table/plot, PCA plot, distance heatmap, verdict text) are saved as files in the step's output directory

plan.title: AD skin RNA-seq: QC, PCA, sample distances
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is a 12000x13 raw gene-level count matrix from Salmon (12 skin samples: 6 AD lesional vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch), with a flagged caveat that sample_01 has a library size ~4x below the median. Before any differential expression testing, the research question asks for a pure QC characterization: library sizes per sample, a PCA on normalized/variance-stabilized expression, a sample-to-sample distance matrix (heatmap/hierarchical clustering), and an explicit verdict on sample_01. This is entirely a bulk-RNA-seq QC task on the count matrix and its metadata, so it routes as a single step to the bulk-transcriptomics-agent using standard DESeq2-based size-factor normalization and variance-stabilizing transformation (vst), which is installed in this environment. No pathway, network, or reference data is needed for this step since it is purely descriptive QC on the count matrix itself.
